rachel (sales): Heads up team 5 — enterprise commit signed (12mo). They plan two 15-minute marketing blasts/month that could push traffic from baseline ~600 concurrent to ~2500 concurrent. Ask: recommended reserved GPU commitment, burst/autoscale strategy (spot vs on-demand mix), quick pricing ballpark, and security answers re: prewarm + KMS. Can we outline a playbook?

devin (solutions): Quick proposal framework: reserve for steady-state 95th, provide a prewarmed hot-pool for short spikes, and a larger spot-backed burst pool with automatic fallback rules to a smaller model. Include burst-credit offering on contract.

anita (infra): Important operational constraints: spot provisioning cold-start ~2-6m depending on region, on-demand ~1-3m. Prewarm must be cross-AZ to avoid AZ outage risk. Also need to decide whether prewarm runs in our VPC or customer's VPC for security.

rachel (sales): Customer SLO: 99% of requests <= 200ms token-latency for chat-style completions. Model they plan to use: LlamaX-34B quantized. Avg reply size ~120 tokens, expected average session think-time ~25s during bursts.

ho (eng-runtime): Measured baseline for LlamaX-34B-quant on A100-class nodes with tight batching: ~550-650 tokens/sec per GPU for short sequences if KV cache hits are good. Latency SLO 200ms is tight; we must cap batch delay and tune max-batch-size to keep p99 in range.

devin (solutions): Rough math (peak):
- Peak concurrent sessions = 2500
- Tokens per response = 120
- Inter-request interval = 25s
Tokens/sec needed = 2500 * 120 / 25 = 12,000 tps.
At 600 tps/GPU -> 12,000 / 600 = 20 GPUs. Add 30% headroom for degraded cache hit/batching -> ~26 GPUs to serve peak with latency constraints.
For steady 95th (600 concurrent): 600 * 120 / 25 = 2,880 tps -> ~5 GPUs. So propose reserved commit = 6 GPUs (covers steady + safety), hot prewarm pool = 6 GPUs (always warm, spread across AZs), burst pool capacity = 30 GPUs (mix spot/on-demand) with autoscaler.

anita (infra): Spot strategy: keep prewarmed hot-pool small but enough to absorb short spikes while spot nodes boot. Prewarm per-AZ: 2 GPUs (hot), with a cross-AZ buffer. Configure autoscale to add spot nodes aggressively when queue grows but keep fallback rules to move traffic to hot-pool or smaller model. Also recommend a 10-minute preheat window before planned campaigns.

ho (eng-runtime): Example autoscale & fallback policy (pseudo-yaml):
```
autoscale:
  reserved_commit: 6
  hot_pool_always_on: 6
  burst_pool_max: 30
  burst_mix: { spot: 0.7, on_demand: 0.3 }
  scale_trigger: token_queue_ms > 100
  scale_step: 4_gpus
  cool_down: 45s
  prewarm_schedule: campaign_window - 10m
  fallback_model: llamaX-13B-quant
  throttles: { per_user_rps: 1, global_qps_limit: 12000 }
```
Notes: fallback_model used when queue latency cannot be reduced quickly; throttles protect backend and reduce p99 latency risk.

devin (solutions): Pricing sketch (placeholder numbers to be refined after microbench):
- Reserved commit: 6 x A100-equivalent @ $8,000/mo/GPU = $48k/mo commit
- Hot prewarm pool included in commit (6 GPUs)
- Burst usage: up to 30 GPUs billed hourly; on-demand @ $3/hr/GPU, spot @ $1.2/hr/GPU (example)
- Offer onboarding burst credits: 150 GPU-hours to cover first-month campaigns
We should convert to $/1k requests after we run the benchmark with their prompt mix.

rachel (sales): Security Qs they raised: customer-managed keys for model inputs, audit trail for prewarm payloads, and whether prewarm content persists beyond cache TTL.

anita (infra): Hosted enterprise can be configured with customer-managed KMS (envelope encryption). Prewarm jobs can run in customer VPC for Private deployments. Prewarm payloads are treated as ephemeral: KV cache is encrypted at rest, TTL is short (configurable), and we can enable auditing for prewarm runs (who/what payloads).

h o (eng-runtime): Clarification: we do not write raw prompts to long-term object stores for prewarm. Cache is ephemeral, encrypted, and we can scrub and anonymize prefixes before prewarming. We can provide audit logs (time, job id, prewarm-hash) for compliance reviews.

sec-bot: Created POC workspace "blast-poc-212346" scheduled 2026-04-10 -> 2026-04-17. Owners: rachel, devin, anita.

rachel (sales): Action items: (1) Ho/infra to run a microbench with their prompt set and return per-GPU tps+latency table by Tue EOD. (2) Anita to prepare prewarm-in-VPC template + AZ distribution + cold-start timelines. (3) Devin to draft formal pricing proposal with burst-credit options. (4) I'll send the security questionnaire and request KMS proof points.

devin (solutions): I'll also draft an emergency runbook: how to flip traffic to 13B, enable global throttles, and consume burst credits during a campaign.

ho (eng-runtime): I'll include a script to simulate the 15-min spike and a dashboard template (token-based queues, p50/p95/p99 latency) for the POC.

anita (infra): I'll add recommended SLA notes: prewarm recommendation: start prewarm 10m before campaign, maintain hot-pool across AZs, and have one on-call for campaign windows.

rachel (sales): Great work. We'll follow up after bench results. :rocket:
